rows: If efficient and feasible, give the code the intended and safe semantics (i.e., make the code do the right and safe thing) “Efficient” can include providing guarantees (or evidence such as binary object comparison) of functionality and performance Such a semantic improvement should always apply to both “enforced” and “non-enforced” mode, so that code that compiles cleanly in both modes means the same thing
“Holy grail”: Automatically fixes bugs in existing code just by recompiling the code Plus some cases can perform reliable automatic source M modernization
Diagnose violations at compile time, and where possible provide a clear “use this instead” correction This is always “Ill-Formed, Diagnostic Required”
“If it compiles then it’s safe” Plus some cases can perform reliable automatic source M modernization
Violations must be addressed by manual or automatic code changes
Where necessary, diagnose violations at run time, and let the program customize how violations are handled (ideally the same as contract group violation handlers, once those are available)
Automatically diagnoses bugs in existing code just by recompiling the code
